Settle the Curvature of an iwls() Against a Family

Source: R/iwls.R
iwls_resolve.Rd

Turns the information of an iwls() into the matrix that a fit runs. With information given, that object replaces the one that the method holds; without it, a method that holds an unsettled auto_info() is settled and a method whose curvature was named is returned as it is.

Usage

iwls_resolve(method, distrib, information = NULL)

Arguments

method

An Iwls() object.

distrib

The distribution to which the model is fitted.

information

NULL, or an object that inherits from distributions7::Information that replaces the one of method.

Value

An Iwls() object whose hessian is an distributions7::expected_info() or an distributions7::observed_info() object, unless a named choice is returned as it is.

Details

A named distributions7::observed_info() or distributions7::expected_info() is the matrix of the step and nothing else: the method carries no fallback and no switch.

An auto_info() is settled by two questions. distributions7::expected_hessian_exact() is the first. Where it returns FALSE the expected information is an approximation, the outer product of the scores by default, and the method is settled on the observed information, with the expected information as the backup that takes the step where the observed step finds no acceptable point. An observed penalized information that is not positive definite is first floored by pd_repair() and its step tried.

distributions7::expected_hessian_costly() is the second question. A family whose expected information is exact but costly is settled on the observed information as well, because the expected information of such a family requires a quadrature or a sum over the support at each observation. The expected information is the backup there too.

Only a family settled on the expected information has switching set.

See also

iwls(), fit_smooth(), which reads backup.
